name: Kong Inc. (formerly Mashape)
origin_detail: Founded in Milan in 2009 as Mashape by schoolmates Augusto 'Aghi' Marietti and Marco Palladino; now headquartered in San Francisco. Per the company timeline, after open-sourcing its API gateway it named it Kong (2017-2019 period).
openness_notes: Kong Gateway is Apache-2.0 (GitHub); the commercial Konnect subscription adds functionality. Open core throughout, and no core relicensing was found in fetched pages.

license_history.note: Open-sourcing year not confirmed in fetched pages.

robustness: Apache-2.0 gateway built on NGINX/OpenResty, so forkable; a single vendor controls the roadmap. The README describes Konnect as adding functionality, and mentions no removal of open-source features.
openness_effect_assessment: Kong kept a stable Apache-2.0 open core with no core relicensing found, and still raised at rising valuations ($1.4B in 2021, $2B in 2023). In API infrastructure, at least, an unchanged permissive core coexisted with growing private valuations.
key_takeaway: Kong is the 'stable open core' control case: Apache-2.0 gateway, paid enterprise features and SaaS, no licence change found, and private valuations rising from $1.4B (2021) to $2B (2023). It contrasts with the database companies that relicensed their cores.
